title: multi-action button
desc: multi-action button / interaction
author: @nickpylll
summary: Mobile fintech FAB that expands into a vertical action menu (Receive/Send/Swap) with staggered spring entrances over a blurred backdrop, then collapses back.

frames.desc: Resting: home screen with balance card; black circular FAB with white plus bottom-right; background sharp.
Tap FAB: backdrop blurs and dims; first item 'Receive' (orange download icon) pops in above FAB with overshoot.
'Send' (purple paper-plane) and 'Swap' (blue arrows) cascade in, staggered ~75ms, each scaling 0.5->1 with spring; labels slide in from the right.
Menu fully open and settled; backdrop stays blurred.
Collapse: items fade/shrink in reverse stagger, labels exit first, icons scale to ~0.3 drifting toward the FAB origin.
Backdrop un-blurs; plus icon returns (rotated back). Loop.

mechanics.timing: open ~450ms with 60-90ms stagger; close ~300ms reverse stagger

prompt:
Rebuild this interaction 1:1: a mobile fintech FAB that expands into a vertical action menu (Receive / Send / Swap) with staggered spring entrances over a blurred, dimmed backdrop, then collapses back to the plus.

## Integration
Integration: stack-agnostic spec - springs given as stiffness/damping, timed motions as duration + curve, canvas/shader notes are perf guidance only; map every value to your framework and animation library of choice.

## Scene
Mobile home screen with a balance card. Bottom-right: 56px black circular FAB with a white plus. Menu items stack vertically above the FAB: Receive (orange download icon), Send (purple paper-plane), Swap (blue arrows) - each a row with 40px circular icon tile + label to its right.

## Motion spec
Pattern: entrance/exit with stagger choreography.
- Open trigger: tap FAB. Backdrop layer blurs (backdrop-filter blur 12px) and dims (black/30) over 300ms.
- FAB plus rotates to close (0 -> 45deg, 250ms ease-out).
- Items enter: scale 0.5 -> 1, y +12 -> 0, opacity 0 -> 1, spring overshoot cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1); stagger 60-90ms between items, Receive first. Labels slide in from the right (x +8 -> 0) with their icon.
- Full open settles ~450ms after tap.
- Close: labels exit first, icons scale to 0.3 while drifting toward the FAB origin, reverse stagger, total ~300ms, ease-in. Backdrop un-blurs; plus rotates back.

## Calibration
- The overshoot spring (0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1) is the character of this menu - do not substitute a plain ease-out.
- Stagger 60-90ms: under 50ms reads as simultaneous, over 120ms reads as laggy.
- Close is ~30% faster than open (300 vs 450ms).

## Reduced motion
No spring, no stagger: menu fades in/out as one group, 150ms opacity only. Backdrop still dims (no blur).

## Don't miss
- Items drift toward the FAB origin as they collapse - they do not fade in place.
- The blur lives on a separate backdrop layer behind the menu, never on the page content itself.
- Labels move independently from icon tiles; that separation is what makes the cascade feel choreographed.

prompt:
Rebuild this interaction 1:1: a static 4-card bento portfolio grid orbited by a single thick white stroke that continuously draws itself along a rounded scribble path looping around and between the cards, comet-style. The cards never move.

## Integration
Integration: stack-agnostic spec - springs given as stiffness/damping, timed motions as duration + curve, canvas/shader notes are perf guidance only; map every value to your framework and animation library of choice.

## Scene
Bento grid, 24px card rounding, small even gaps: tall orange "Product UI & web" card left; pink "Icons" top-right; yellow "Illustrations" below it; wide purple "AI Design Setup" spanning the bottom. Over the whole grid, one SVG path that tours the cards' perimeters and the gaps between them, its corners rounded to match the 24px card radius.

## Motion spec
Pattern: autoplay loop, single animated property.
- The stroke: 6-8px white rounded-cap segment, ~25-35% of the total path length visible at any time.
- Implement as a moving dash window: path with stroke-dasharray equal to [visible arc, remainder], animate stroke-dashoffset linearly so the segment travels the full circuit in ~6s, constant speed.
- Head leads, tail follows at fixed arc length; the segment sweeps around card edges and threads the gaps between cards.
- No other motion: cards, colors, and layout are perfectly still. No easing - linear throughout.

## Calibration
- Full circuit ~6s. Faster reads as a loading spinner; slower stops registering as motion.
- The segment length (25-35% of path) is what makes it read as a comet, not a drawing-on outline.
- Round the path's corners to exactly the card radius (24px) so the stroke hugs the cards.

## Reduced motion
Stroke renders static as a full closed outline at low opacity (white/40), no travel.

## Don't miss
- One continuous path for the whole grid - not per-card outlines animating separately.
- The stroke passes through the gaps between cards, weaving; a pure perimeter trace looks wrong.
- Constant linear speed, including around corners.

title: Follower Count
desc: Follower Count
author: @AdityaSur11
summary: Slider-driven crowd visualization: dragging 0->5,000+ spawns illustrated people sprites that pack into a dense crowd whose silhouette morphs (ellipse blob -> twin-lobe heart) as the count grows.

frames.desc: Empty canvas, slider at 0, pill counter reads 0-2; one or two people sprites center.
Slider ~40%: dense elliptical crowd blob center-canvas, hundreds of distinct figures packed; pill ~2,000.
Slider ~70%: crowd wider than tall; pill ~5,000; silhouette still a rounded mass.
Crowd reorganizes into two distinct lobes, left lobe first.
Twin-lobe heart/clover silhouette fully formed and packed; pill 5,000+.
Slider releases back toward 0; crowd thins to one figure; loop.

elements: 10-20 unique person sprite variants instanced thousands of times
mechanics.easing: layout ease-out; new sprites pop scale 0->1 150ms

prompt:
Rebuild this interaction 1:1: a slider-driven crowd visualization. Dragging 0 -> 5,000+ spawns illustrated people sprites that pack into a dense crowd whose silhouette morphs from an ellipse blob into a twin-lobe heart as the count grows. A black pill counter rolls like an odometer.

## Integration
Integration: stack-agnostic spec - springs given as stiffness/damping, timed motions as duration + curve, canvas/shader notes are perf guidance only; map every value to your framework and animation library of choice.

## Scene
Light canvas. Bottom: slider with tick marks and a draggable knob. Top or floating: black pill with the live count in white tabular digits. Canvas center: the crowd.

## Motion spec
Pattern: gesture-driven scrub with lagged layout.
- Scrub 1:1 with the drag: count maps slider position 0-100% to 0-5,000+.
- Sprites: entering figures pop scale 0 -> 1 in 150ms; crowd positions ease toward their packed targets ~300ms behind the slider (ease-out) - the crowd visibly chases the count.
- Silhouette keyframes: sparse (~0-500) a few figures center; ~2,000 a dense elliptical blob; ~5,000 wider than tall; 5,000+ reorganizes into two distinct lobes (left lobe forms first), resolving to a twin-lobe heart/clover.
- Pill counter: digits roll vertically like an odometer, ~200ms per change, tabular-nums.
- Release at the top: slider auto-returns toward 0 and the crowd thins back to one figure.

## Calibration
- The ~300ms position lag is the soul of the piece - the crowd feels like it has mass.
- Pop-in 150ms per new sprite; faster is invisible, longer turns into popcorn.
- Odometer rolls, never text swaps; digit height equals the pill's font size.

## Reduced motion
Sprites appear/disappear without pop or travel; silhouettes crossfade between keyframes, 150ms opacity. Counter swaps without rolling.

## Don't miss
- Thousands of instances need instancing/canvas - DOM nodes per person will not hold 60fps.
- The morph blob -> twin lobes must be a reorganization of the same figures, not two images crossfading.
- Left lobe forms first, right follows - the asymmetry is in the reference.

title: Time for different time zones

Drag: ticks stream horizontally; orange band grows right of NOW labeled '-1H 15M'; row times roll like odometers; statuses flip.
Band widens to '-6H 40M'..'-7H'; day labels flip to YESTERDAY for cities crossing midnight.
Band settles ~-9H; final scrubbed times and updated status icons.
Release: ruler springs back to NOW, band collapses; times roll back up; statuses revert.
Resting state restored. One frame shows New Delhi dragged above New York - row reorder gesture.

prompt:
Rebuild this interaction 1:1: a dark world-clock app with a scrubbable 24h tick ruler. Dragging horizontally shifts time globally - every city row rolls its odometer clock, an orange selection band shows the scrubbed window with live duration, day/status labels update across midnight. Release springs back to NOW. Rows can also be drag-reordered vertically.

## Integration
Integration: stack-agnostic spec - springs given as stiffness/damping, timed motions as duration + curve, canvas/shader notes are perf guidance only; map every value to your framework and animation library of choice.

## Scene
Dark UI (near-black bg, white text). Top: horizontal tick ruler (hour ticks, minor/major) with a red NOW marker fixed center. Right of NOW while scrubbing: orange selection band with a mono duration label ("-6H 40M"). Below: city rows (Warsaw, SF -9H, NY -6H, New Delhi +3H30M) each with name, offset badge, day chip (TODAY/YESTERDAY), status icon (night/working), and HH:MM rolling clock.

## Motion spec
Pattern: gesture-driven scrub + spring release; plus vertical drag-reorder.
- Horizontal drag: ruler translateX 1:1 under the finger; band grows from NOW with live duration label; all rows' digits roll continuously (~200ms roll cadence); day chips flip to YESTERDAY as cities cross midnight; status icons flip with working hours.
- Release: ruler springs back to NOW (stiffness ~170, damping ~22, ~500ms settle); band collapses; digits roll back up; statuses revert.
- Vertical drag on a row: row lifts (scale 1.02, shadow), siblings slide aside with layout animations, drop reorders.

## Calibration
- Scrub is 1:1 and immediate - any smoothing on the ruler itself kills the directness; smoothing lives only in the digit rolls.
- Release spring ~500ms settle with a soft overshoot; stiffness 170 / damping 22 is the reference feel.
- Digit rolls ~200ms, always rolling in the direction of travel.

## Reduced motion
Ruler still scrubs 1:1 (it is positional, not decorative); digits swap without rolling; release uses a 200ms ease-out tween instead of spring.

## Don't miss
- NOW marker stays pinned; the ruler moves under it - never move the marker.
- The band is anchored at NOW and grows in the drag direction, labeled live.
- Reorder and time-scrub are separate gestures on separate axes; do not let horizontal jitter reorder rows.

title: boarding pass printer
desc: boarding pass printer
author: @heydamir
summary: A boarding pass 'prints' out of a slot at the top of a phone screen like a thermal printer - ticket feeds down into view, sways gently, then retracts; infinite loop.

frames.desc: 'Upcoming Trip' screen; dark printer slot near top; only the barcode stub of the pass peeking out.
Pass feeds downward: route header, date, passenger, gate/seat rows reveal top-to-bottom like paper from a printer; soft shadow grows under the leading edge.
Pass fully printed, hanging from slot: pendulum sway (+-1.5deg) and micro settle bounce; perforated bottom edge + barcode visible.
Retract: pass slides back up into the slot; shadow shrinks.
Slot nearly empty; brief pause.
Next print cycle starts; loop.

mechanics.timing: feed ~1.6s, hold ~1.2s with sway, retract ~1s, pause 600ms
mechanics.easing: feed cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1); sway sine 2.5s; retract ease-in

prompt:
Rebuild this interaction 1:1: a boarding pass that "prints" out of a dark slot at the top of a phone screen like a thermal printer - the ticket feeds down into view, sways gently while hanging, then retracts. Infinite loop.

## Integration
Integration: stack-agnostic spec - springs given as stiffness/damping, timed motions as duration + curve, canvas/shader notes are perf guidance only; map every value to your framework and animation library of choice.

## Scene
"Upcoming Trip" phone screen. Near the top: a dark horizontal printer slot bar. The pass: white card with route header, date, passenger, gate/seat rows, perforated bottom edge and barcode. A soft drop shadow under the pass's leading edge.

## Motion spec
Pattern: autoplay loop with four beats.
- Feed (~1.6s, cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1)): the pass emerges top-first from the slot - only the barcode stub peeks out at rest; content reveals top-to-bottom as paper would. Shadow grows (opacity and scale) under the leading edge.
- Hold (~1.2s): fully printed, hanging from the slot. Pendulum sway +/-1.5deg on a 2.5s sine, with a micro settle bounce as the feed stops.
- Retract (~1s, ease-in): pass slides back up into the slot; shadow shrinks.
- Pause 600ms with the slot nearly empty, then the next print cycle begins.

## Calibration
- Feed easing (0.65, 0, 0.35, 1) gives the mechanical, motor-driven feel - a soft ease-out reads as a UI slide, not printing.
- Sway amplitude +/-1.5deg max; this is paper on air, not a swing.
- Retract is faster than feed (1s vs 1.6s).

## Reduced motion
Feed and retract as opacity+short-translate tweens (300ms); no pendulum sway.

## Don't miss
- The pass is clipped by the slot window the whole time - it must look fed, not dropped in.
- The shadow is tied to the leading edge and grows during the feed; it sells the physicality.
- The perforated bottom edge and barcode are visible during the hold - they are the realism cue.

title: Deploy Pipeline

author: @jeetnirnejak

Build completes: node flips green with white check; connector segment Build->Test fills green; Test node activates (orange spinner). Elapsed timer ticking in footer.
Test running: log panel shows test output lines appearing one by one; Test row highlighted in list.
Test green-checked; Preview activates. Each transition: check draws in with a small pop, next node scales up slightly on activation.
Preview green; Production running (orange). Log shows deploy lines ('uploading assets', 'flushing edge cache').
All 4 nodes green; header status flips to 'Deployed' (green dot); footer button morphs from disabled to black 'Re-deploy'; loop restarts.

prompt:
Rebuild this interaction 1:1: a CI/CD "Deploy Pipeline" card where a 4-stage stepper (Build -> Test -> Preview -> Production) advances left to right on its own, logs stream below, and the card ends in a "Deployed" state with a Re-deploy button. Then it loops.

## Integration
Integration: stack-agnostic spec - springs given as stiffness/damping, timed motions as duration + curve, canvas/shader notes are perf guidance only; map every value to your framework and animation library of choice.

## Scene
White card, radius 16, border black/8, padding 24. Header row: bold title "Deploy Pipeline", mono branch+commit chip ("main a3f7c1d", 11px, grey/50 bg), status pill right ("Running: <stage>" orange dot + text; "Deployed" green). Body: horizontal stepper, 4 circular 40px icon nodes joined by a 2px track (#e4e4e7). Below: stage list (4 rows, icon + name + state), then a log panel (mono 12px, zinc-500, max 6 lines), footer with elapsed timer left and action button right.

## Motion spec
Pattern: autoplay scripted sequence.
- Node states: idle (grey outline, 40% opacity) / active (orange fill, scale 1 -> 1.08 spring stiffness 300 damping 20, spinning conic-gradient ring via background-image rotation, 1s linear infinite) / done (green fill, white SVG check draws in via stroke-dashoffset over 250ms ease-out with a 1.1 -> 1 scale pop).
- Track fill: separate green bar, scaleX 0 -> 1 origin-left, 400ms ease-out, behind the nodes, segment by segment as each stage completes.
- Stage timing: Build 2s, Test 2.5s, Preview 2s, Production 1.5s (full run ~9s).
- Log lines: append one per 300-400ms while a stage runs; each enters opacity 0 -> 1, y 4 -> 0, 200ms ease-out.
- Finish: header pill flips to "Deployed" (crossfade 200ms), footer button morphs from disabled grey to solid black "Re-deploy" (background + text crossfade, 250ms).
- Hold Deployed 1.5s, then reset all nodes to idle (300ms fade) and restart.

## Calibration
- Transitions 200-400ms, all ease-out cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); timer counts linearly.
- The check pop and the next-node scale-up are the two moments that make it feel alive - keep them snappy (under 300ms).
- Only the active node's ring spins; idle/done nodes are perfectly still.

## Reduced motion
No spinning rings, no pop. Stage changes fade opacity only, 150ms. Timer and logs still update.

## Don't miss
- The connector fills behind the nodes, not through them.
- Check draws in as a stroke, not a fade-in of the whole icon.
- The Re-deploy button morphs in place; it does not appear elsewhere.

Rebuild these 4 static product UI comps 1:1, pixel-faithful: dark-mode marketing screenshots of (1) an audio signal dashboard, (2) a CRM filters panel, (3) a command-K palette, (4) an AI chat citation popover. Fidelity is the deliverable - there is no motion.

## Integration
Integration: stack-agnostic spec - every value is plain layout/typography/CSS; recreate with your own components and assets.

## Layout
Each comp is a dark panel floating over a photographic backdrop with real backdrop blur. Comp 1 "Threshold / Signal strength": dark panel over a motion-blurred grass photo. Comp 2 "Filters": dark slide-over over a blurred warm photo. Comp 3: glassy command palette over a wheat-field photo. Comp 4: AI answer card over article text.

- Comp 1: huge numerals 56.2% / 43.8%, +32% delta chip, yellow segmented progress bar with tick labels 0-100%, ACTIVE CHANNELS row with 4 small icons + "4 INPUTS" chip, corner reticle marks on the panel.

## Typography & color
Dark theme: near-black surfaces, white primary text, zinc-500 secondary, mono for numbers and kbd hints (tabular-nums), semibold titles, tight tracking on the big numerals. Glass panels: border white/10, never solid gray.

## States
Static comps. If interactive behavior is wanted, restrict it to a 120ms hover background on interactive rows.

## Don't miss

- Corner reticle marks on comp 1 and presence dots in comp 3 are the details people notice.

prompt:
Rebuild this flow 1:1: a marketing-to-product journey for "Wafer" (serverless LLM hosting). Four screens: a cinematic auth screen over a dithered classical seascape, an app shell with icon rail, an onboarding flow (model picker, plan pricing rows, API-key step), and a dashboard glimpse - then it loops back out to the artwork.

## Integration
Integration: stack-agnostic spec - every value is plain CSS/layout/typography; reveals are described as durations + cubic-bezier curves that map to any animation library or CSS transitions.

## Screen 1 - Auth
Backdrop: classical seascape painting converted to heavy 1-bit dither, full-bleed. Center: dark auth card - email input, GitHub and Google SSO buttons, "Create an account" primary button. Browser-chrome framing around the scene.

## Screen 2 - App shell
Left icon rail (wafer logo, Home, API keys, Billing, Usage, Docs, Team) over a dark app surface; centered welcome: "Welcome to Wafer. Let's set up your serverless LLM."

## Screen 3 - Onboarding
Stacked steps: model picker (dark card, radio + sparkle icon); plan rows with prices per 1M tokens ($3.00 / $15.00 / $0.30...) in mono tabular figures; API-key step - dark code block with syntax-highlighted curl/JS snippet and a "Create key" toggle that flips green when on.

## Screen 4 - Dashboard + exit
More plan tiers scroll past; a brief "Unlimited?..." modal appears at the top; then the journey reverses out to the pure dithered seascape and restarts.

## Transitions
- Auth -> app shell: card crossfades into the shell, 400ms.
- Section reveals within onboarding: opacity 0 -> 1, y 16 -> 0, 500ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), fired as each section enters view.
- Pricing rows stagger ~80ms, laid down by the scroll.
- Toggle flip: green fill, 200ms.
- Exit: crossfade to the artwork alone, 400ms.

## Calibration
- Reveals are generous but restrained: 500ms, 16px of rise, no scale, no bounce.
- The dither texture is static throughout - the art is the constant, the UI moves.
- The full walkthrough runs ~39s at demo pace.

## Reduced motion
All reveals become opacity-only, 150ms, no rise; sections render immediately.

## Don't miss
- The dithered painting frames both ends of the journey; never cover it edge-to-edge with UI.
- The icon rail appears with the app shell and stays - it anchors every product screen.
- Plan rows are quiet lists in mono, not cards-in-cards; the toggle's green flip is the only saturated moment in onboarding.

title: Dither Cards
desc: Dither Cards
author: @praveenisomer
summary: Two editorial art cards side by side ('Capital Metamorphosis' flower, 'Sensitive Dependencies' insect) rendered in black-and-white dither; the insect image morphs through metamorphosis stages (bee -> curled larva -> dark chrysalis -> butterfly) while a bottom progress bar + color-ring indicator cycle.

frames.desc: Two tall white cards on a grey dithered backdrop; left card static purple-tinted dithered flower, right card shows a dithered bee; captions + pink tags below images; bottom row has a rainbow conic ring and a track bar.
Right image crossfades/morphs to a curled creature pose; dither pattern stays crisp at all times (no blur).
Right image morphs again into an abstract dark crumpled form (chrysalis); left flower cycles its own subtle bloom variants.
Right image resolves into a fully-formed butterfly; progress bar has advanced steadily; ring hue rotates.

prompt:
Rebuild this interaction 1:1: two editorial art cards rendered in crisp black-and-white dither. The right card's image morphs through metamorphosis stages (bee -> curled larva -> dark chrysalis -> butterfly) on an infinite loop while a bottom progress bar fills and a conic ring rotates hue. The left card cycles subtle bloom variants of a dithered flower.

## Integration
Integration: stack-agnostic spec - springs given as stiffness/damping, timed motions as duration + curve, canvas/shader notes are perf guidance only; map every value to your framework and animation library of choice.

## Scene
Grey dithered backdrop. Two tall white cards, radius 12, border black/5. Each card: 3:4 image area, caption "Title / subtitle" (semibold 14px / zinc-500 12px), small pink tag chips, footer row with a 16px conic-gradient ring indicator and a 2px progress track. Prepare 4 plates of the same subject converted to 1-bit ordered dithering (Bayer 4x4) at identical dimensions.

## Motion spec
Pattern: autoplay loop (no interaction).
- Plate cycle: each plate holds ~1.5s, crossfade 400ms ease-in-out to the next (or threshold dissolve: pixels flip in dither-noise order over 400ms - crunchier and more on-theme).
- Full metamorphosis: ~6s across 4 plates.
- Progress bar: scaleX 0 -> 1 across the full 6s cycle, linear, origin left; returns to 0 on reset.
- Conic ring: hue rotates 360deg over the same 6s, linear.
- Left card: cycles its own subtle bloom variants on the same clock, offset by half a cycle.
- Reset: butterfly crossfades back to the bee (400ms), bar and ring snap to zero; loop restarts immediately.

## Calibration
- Crossfades 400ms - shorter flickers, longer muddies the dither texture.
- The dither must stay crisp at all times: images pixel-aligned, no blur filters, image-rendering: pixelated.
- Bar and ring are ambient, perfectly linear - they are clocks, not actors.

## Reduced motion
Hold on the first plate of each card. Bar and ring render static at 0.

## Don't miss
- All 4 plates must share exact dimensions and subject registration, or the morph looks like a slideshow.
- Pair the two cards: left card is the calm control, right card is the one that transforms.
- The ring hue rotation and bar fill share one clock - they must never drift apart.

Each stamp has serrated die-cut edges framing soft aurora shader art (green "SEASON QUIT", terracotta "SUDDEN SNEAK", blue "AIRFLOW", black "SIGHT COUNTER" 01/2025). Warm beige field. Horizontal strip of stamps: center stamp large with its title and aurora art visible; receding stamps progressively smaller, blurred, desaturated. Small cursor near center.

Pattern: infinite coverflow glide + drag.

prompt:
Rebuild this interaction 1:1: "toss your note to the bin" - a playful pull-down-to-delete gesture in an iPhone notes app. Pull down and the sticky note crumples into a paper ball; the scene swaps to a sketched wire-mesh trash can; release flings the ball on a ballistic arc into the bin with a rim bounce and bin jiggle; then cut back to the notes grid, note gone.

## Integration
Integration: stack-agnostic spec - springs given as stiffness/damping, timed motions as duration + curve, canvas/shader notes are perf guidance only; map every value to your framework and animation library of choice.

## Scene
iPhone-frame note editor: pink sticky note card (radius 16, rotation -1deg, hand-drawn heart-arrow scribble, note text), color swatch row, tag chips, bottom action bar (copy/share/draw/trash). Toss scene: white field, sketched grey wire-mesh trash can upper-center (line-art, slight 3D tilt ~10deg), hint text "Pull down to aim your toss" 12px zinc-400.

## Motion spec
Pattern: gesture-driven with ballistic release.
- Crumple (drag 0 -> 60px): crossfade to the white toss scene, 200ms. Note border-radius 16 -> 50%, scale 1 -> 0.45, crinkle texture overlay fades in, random +/-2deg rotation jitter keyed to drag distance. All crumple progress is tied directly to drag y (scrubbed, not timed).
- Aim (drag held past 60px): ball sticks to the finger with rubber-band factor 0.85 (ball lags the finger 15%); "aim" hint pulses opacity 1 -> 0.5 -> 1 on a 1.2s loop; ball sways with horizontal drag.
- Release: compute velocity from the last 100ms of drag; launch the ball on a 2D projectile arc (gravity 2400px/s2) toward the bin mouth, ~700ms flight. On entry the ball scales into the bin (clip), the bin jiggles (rotate +/-4deg, spring stiffness 400 damping 12, ~600ms), small "puff" opacity burst at the rim.
- Finish: hard cut (no transition) back to the notes grid; the deleted card is already gone.

## Calibration
- The crumple is scrubbed to the finger - no independent timing; that directness is what makes it feel physical.
- Toss duration comes from real projectile math, not a fixed keyframe; a weak flick should still land (aim assist: clamp the arc to the bin mouth within +/-20deg).
- Bin jiggle is the payoff - springy and brief, under 700ms.

## Reduced motion
Pull-down shows a static "release to delete" state; on release the ball fades into the bin (opacity only, 200ms), no arc, no jiggle.

## Don't miss
- The scene swap happens at the 60px threshold, mid-gesture, not on release.
- The ball lags the finger slightly (rubber-band) - a 1:1 stick feels dead.
- The return to the notes grid is a hard cut after the dunk, not a crossfade; the contrast is the joke landing.
